source.title: The Inductive Bias of Convolutional Neural Networks: Locality and Weight Sharing Reshape Implicit Regularization
source.authors: Tong-Tong Liang; Esha Singh; Rahul Parhi; Alexander Cloninger; Yu-Xiang Wang

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper. It has some garbled mathematical notation and figure/table extraction, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies full-batch gradient descent, squared training loss, and Hessian sharpness near the edge-of-stability threshold, using two-layer ReLU networks. This bears on part of V5, though it does not test learning rates above the threshold described there.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 results are noisy-label regression with squared loss, not classification error. The paper also discusses prior studies, but those cited results are not recorded as rows. Figure-only numerical values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own training-loss and Hessian-sharpness trajectories in two-layer regression networks. These bear on V5's full-batch edge-of-stability component in new architecture and data settings. Regression loss is the relevant measure for this component; classification error is unnecessary.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that sparse connectivity shifts stability-induced regularization to patch geometry: concentrated patches can yield meaningful generalization guarantees, whereas isolatable patches permit stable memorization. Their analysis concerns two-layer regression networks; extension to deep networks remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes two-layer ReLU regression networks under full-batch gradient descent, with squared loss and a stability constraint. It does not use the classification training recipes in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Patch geometry changes whether the sparsely connected network interpolates noisy labels: random spherical patches permit interpolation, while the CIFAR-10 patch setting stabilizes near the noise floor. In the CIFAR-10 experiment, the fully connected comparator interpolates while the sparse network does not.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparse connectivity and patch geometry determine whether stability constraints prevent noise fitting: the CIFAR-10 SCN remains near the noise floor while the FCN interpolates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In two-layer squared-loss regression, patch geometry governs whether sparse connectivity prevents noise interpolation under stability-constrained training.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 4.2 and 4.3 establish generalization bounds for structured patch geometry and the existence of stable interpolants for isolatable patches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Below-threshold sharpness alone does not guarantee generalization; its implications depend on architecture and patch geometry.

record.problems: The experimental findings relevant to training loss and sharpness are presented in figures rather than tables or numerical result text; exact values and uncertainty for those curves cannot be extracted. The experiments use two-layer regression models, not classification benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: No rows kept. The relevant Figure 3 and Figure 5 outcomes are figure-based, and the versions’ stated measures do not match the paper’s regression outcomes; Figure 3 and Figure 5 descriptions are summarized under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on capacity or training recipe.
Spurious local minima and the effect of adding one or two student neurons relative to teacher width.
Depth degradation, residual shortcuts, deep plain tanh networks, and normalization-free residual training.
Comparative effects of initialization on training speed and trainable depth.

Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, transient loss increase with curvature reduction, divergence at larger rates, and divergence despite initially subthreshold rates. The experiments do not establish these initial-threshold comparisons.
Batch normalization's effects on speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

missing.what: FCN training-loss and sharpness results: final reported training loss 0.0006, with sharpness described as saturating at the stability threshold over 30,000 epochs. These directly bear on V5 and are not declared in rows_left_out.
missing.locator: Appendix G, Figure 7; training recipe in G.1

missing.what: SCN training-loss and sharpness results: final reported training loss 0.8523, with the caption describing threshold saturation. Record the trajectory qualitatively and distinguish its noise-floor plateau from continued progress toward interpolation.
missing.locator: Appendix G, Figure 6; training recipe in G.1

record.verdict_notes: There are no existing rows to fix. Figures 3 and 5 are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. Their qualitative descriptions still support verdicts without precise curve extraction. Figures 3 and 5 use gradient clipping, so they do not independently establish vanilla-GD dynamics. The CIFAR-10 SCN's loss plateau does not challenge V5, which does not promise interpolation for every architecture and dataset.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 classification training error, corrupted or random classification labels, and the effects of model size, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student spurious local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth, identity shortcuts, very deep plain networks, and normalization-free residual networks.
Initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth, including orthogonal and Gaussian initializations.

The paper measures sharpness around the stability threshold and training loss under full-batch gradient descent, but does not test learning rates above the stability limit of an initial linearized model, report the transient loss rise and recovery in that setting, or test divergence at larger rates. Its threshold-related observations are figure-only and lack precise textual values suitable for result rows.
Batch normalization’s effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

relationships.condition: Synthetic spherical inputs; two-layer FCN trained with full-batch GD at learning rate 0.2 for 30,000 epochs.
relationships.reason: Based on text and Figure 7, with no extracted row ids: sharpness saturates near the stability threshold while training loss approaches zero, with final reported loss 0.0006.
relationships.display_finding: Sharpness saturated near the stability threshold as training loss approached zero, ending at 0.0006.

relationships.condition: Random spherical-patch SCN and CIFAR-10 regression FCN; full-batch updates with gradient clipping at learning rate 0.2.
relationships.reason: Based on Sections 4.3 and 5 and Figures 3 and 5, with no extracted row ids: training reaches interpolation while sharpness hovers near 2/η ≈ 10; the clipping recipe qualifies this evidence.
relationships.display_finding: Training with gradient clipping reached interpolation while sharpness hovered near 2/η ≈ 10.
